subject: Finalize model shortlist + baseline token forecast — NovusHealth ramp
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@novushealth.com>, Chris Tang <chris.tang@novushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovusHealth ramp — model shortlist + draft token profile

Hi Leah / Chris —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. As promised, I’m sending a concise summary of the model shortlist we recommend for your initial clinical-docs summarization and triage flow, plus a baseline token-volume estimate so we can size a dedicated pool for the first 90 days. Attached: model_shortlist_v2.pdf and a starter token estimate workbook.

High-level recommendations (we can walk through live if helpful):
- Primary candidate: Redwood-Compass-13B (quantized) — best balance of cost/latency for 2–6k context where you want reliable structured extraction.
- Secondary (fallback, lower cost): LlamaX-11B-q4 — good for high-throughput low-cost runs when extraction confidence is lower.
- Long-context variant: LlamaX-13B-extended or Redwood-Compass-13B (24k) — for full-encounter summarization use cases.

Token assumptions used in the attached workbook: average incoming context per request 2,400 tokens (patient notes + prior messages), average generation 450 tokens for structured summary + metadata, forecasted peak QPS 3.5 on weekday mornings, optimistic 10% growth week-over-week for ramp.

Next steps I’d like to capture here:
1) Leah/Chris — confirm whether the 2.4k average context matches your telemetry or whether we should use a different baseline.
2) Monica / Grace / Vivek — can you review the attached token estimates and advise whether dedicated capacity or Reserved Dedicated + burst is the right initial plan for Novus?
3) I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync Wednesday to lock model version and SLA targets.

Thanks —
Naomi
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@novushealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Tang <chris.tang@novushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NovusHealth ramp — model shortlist + draft token profile

Hi Naomi —

Thanks — this looks helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
- The 2.4k average context is reasonable for the care-team summarization flow (most notes are ~1.8k, but we frequently attach recent encounter history which bumps it).
- For the triage microflow (shorter prompts), context is typically 400–600 tokens. Those calls are extremely latency-sensitive.
- Peak QPS of 3.5 on mornings seems plausible; on worse days it can hit 5–6 for a 2–3 hour window.

We’re leaning toward starting with a small dedicated pool for the summarization flow and using hosted for the triage microflow; open to your recommendations on model variants for each.

—Leah
Leah Ortiz, Head of Clinical Operations | NovusHealth
leah.ortiz@novushealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: NovusHealth ramp — model shortlist + draft token profile

Thanks Naomi — copying product + infra for sizing inputs. Quick thoughts after a first pass on the workbook:
- If Novus confirms occasional peaks up to 6 QPS for 2–3 hours, we should provision for peak throughput with autoscale headroom. That points to a small Dedicated pool (2 x A100-class) plus burst into hosted.
- Model choices: I agree with Compass-13B quantized as primary for summarize. For the low-latency triage microflow, recommend Redwood-Micro-7B-optimized (fp16) as the primary low-latency candidate — it gives sub-100ms token latency on our infra with tight batching.
- Cost sensitivity: using the hybrid approach (dedicated for heavy summarization, hosted for triage) keeps committed spend reasonable while preserving latency for the microcalls.

Action for eng: Vivek / Rishi, can you run a quick sim using the workbook numbers (attached) and confirm estimated sustained vCPU/GPU hours and expected p95 latency per model variant? We’ll include those numbers in the Novus SOW draft.

Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NovusHealth ramp — model shortlist + draft token profile

Monica —

I ran a quick simulation with the workbook assumptions (attached as a filtered sheet). Key outputs:
- Dedicated pool sizing to hit p95 latency < 400ms for Compass-13B (quantized) at 6 QPS peak: estimate 2x H100 equivalent or 3x A100-80GB (with optimized kernels).
- For the triage microflow with Micro-7B-optimized, hitting sub-100ms p95 requires tight batching and colocated low-latency nodes — we can serve that from hosted nodes but suggest a reserved burst capacity to avoid noisy-neighbor spikes.
- Monthly token estimate (90-day ramp, conservative growth): ~52M input tokens, ~9.6M generated tokens for the summarization flow; triage microflow adds ~8M tokens. Total ~70M token-month for first quarter.
- Cost estimate (ballpark for SOW): $24k–$30k per month depending on committed discount and quantization profile.

Notes: the token workbook includes scenario tabs (baseline / high / low). I attached the filtered outputs; let me know if you want me to produce a slide with capacity curves for the SOW.

-Vivek
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@novushealth.com>, Chris Tang <chris.tang@novushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NovusHealth ramp — model shortlist + draft token profile — recap + next steps

Leah / Chris —

Appreciate the quick feedback and for confirming the context characteristics. Recap / next steps: 
1) Naomi: schedule 30-min sync for Wed 12/8 to finalize model choices and SLA targets (calendar invite sent).
2) Novus: confirm whether you want triage microflow on hosted with reserved burst OR fully dedicated nodes for absolute latency guarantees. If hosted-burst, we’ll include the burst sizing in the SOW.
3) Monica / Vivek: produce a concise SOW appendix that lists the model versions, estimated GPU footprint, and the 90-day token baseline (use the conservative tab). Draft due by Friday 12/4 so we can share with Novus procurement.

Attachments: novus_prod_token_estimates_v1.xlsx, model_shortlist_v2.pdf

If anything above is off, flag it here. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the SOW draft and the Wed sync.

Thanks —
Naomi
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
